images.title: Predict before you multiply
images.purpose: Give a compact recap table that predicts how a product compares with the two numbers from their sizes alone.
images.composition: One 2 by 2 table centred in the frame with row and column headers, generous white space all round; a small multiplication sign in the top left corner cell.
exact_structure: A table of 3 rows and 3 columns of cells in total: the top left cell holds only the sign ×.
Top header row: second cell amber #E69F00 tint with text between 0 and 1, third cell teal #0072B2 tint with text greater than 1.
Left header column: second cell amber #E69F00 tint with text between 0 and 1, third cell teal #0072B2 tint with text greater than 1.

The 4 inner cells: amber row with amber column, vermilion #D55E00 tint, text less than both; amber row with teal column, reddish purple #CC79A7 tint, text in between; teal row with amber column, reddish purple #CC79A7 tint, text in between; teal row with teal column, green #009E73 tint, text greater than both.
Thin dark outlines around every cell; no numbers anywhere in the table.
rejection: more or fewer than 4 inner cells
the cell less than both not at the crossing of the two between 0 and 1 headers
any worked multiplication or numbers added to the table
images.takeaway: Check whether each number is above or below 1, and you know the size of the product before multiplying.
images.description: A 2 by 2 table: between 0 and 1 with between 0 and 1 gives less than both, greater than 1 with greater than 1 gives greater than both, and the mixed cells say in between.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept on predicting the size of a product.
images.teaching_notes: Students should find the row and column for a product's two numbers and read the cell, then check by multiplying.

image_decisions.why: A recap table turns the three situations into a quick prediction tool for practice.
